page.overview:
What is Summanus?

Summanus is a fictional deity created by British author Brian Lumley for his short story "What Dark God?" (, 1975) and identified as a Great Old One in "The Fairground Horror" (, 1976). It is named after an obscure nocturnal thunder god referred to in the works of Ovid, Pliny the Elder, and Martianus Capella.

Appearing as a grotesque, mouthless humanoid with pale tentacles sticking out from under his robes, Summanus can use these appendages to siphon blood from his victims.

Summanus had a following in Roman times, but if he is worshipped today, his cult is even more secretive. The rites needed for the proper worship of Summanus are found in the Tuscan Rituals.

Brian Lumley based this Great Old One on the Roman deity of the same name mentioned in the poet Ovid's Fasti. It first appeared in the short story "What Dark God?" (1975), and was later incorporated into the greater Cthulhu Mythos by Lumley himself in "The Fairground Horror" (1976). Chaosium included it in the Malleus Monstrorum sourcebook for their Call of Cthulhu () roleplaying game.
